∀ (A : Type u) (B : Type v) [Ring A] [Ring B],
  let Bimod := Sigma (fun M : ModuleCat.{w} B =>
    { D : Bimodule.1 B A M // D.1 = (inferInstance : Module B M) })
  let right := fun (M : Bimod) (m : M.1) (a : A) =>
    letI : Module (MulOpposite A) M.1 := M.2.1.2.1
    MulOpposite.op a • m
  let AMod := ModuleCat.{max u x} A
  let BMod := ModuleCat.{max u w x} B
  let regular := ModuleCat.of A (ULift.{x} A)
  let Balanced := fun (M : Bimod) (X : AMod) (Y : BMod)
      (p : ↥M.1 → X → Y) =>
    (∀ m n : ↥M.1, ∀ a : X, p (m + n) a = p m a + p n a) ∧
    (∀ m : ↥M.1, ∀ a b : X, p m (a + b) = p m a + p m b) ∧
    (∀ b : B, ∀ m : ↥M.1, ∀ a : X, p (b • m) a = b • p m a) ∧
    (∀ a : A, ∀ m : ↥M.1, ∀ y : X, p (right M m a) y = p m (a • y))
  let TensorFunctor := fun (M : Bimod) =>
    { D : Sigma (fun F : CategoryTheory.Functor (AMod) (BMod) =>
        ∀ X : AMod, ↥M.1 → X → F.obj X) //
      (∀ X : AMod, Balanced M X (D.1.obj X) (D.2 X)) ∧
      (∀ (X : AMod) (Y : BMod) (p : ↥M.1 → X → Y),
        Balanced M X Y p →
        ∃! k : LinearMap (RingHom.id B) (D.1.obj X) Y,
          ∀ (m : ↥M.1) (y : X), k (D.2 X m y) = p m y) ∧
      (∀ (X Y : AMod) (h : ModuleCat.Hom X Y) (m : ↥M.1) (y : X),
        (ModuleCat.Hom.hom (D.1.map h)) (D.2 X m y) = D.2 Y m ((ModuleCat.Hom.hom h) y)) }
  let NatCode := fun (M N : Bimod) =>
    {f : LinearMap (RingHom.id B) M.1 N.1 //
      ∀ (m : ↥M.1) (a : A), f (right M m a) = right N (f m) a}
  let Component := fun {M N : Bimod}
      (T : TensorFunctor M) (S : TensorFunctor N) (X : AMod) =>
    LinearMap (RingHom.id B) (T.1.1.obj X) (S.1.1.obj X)
  let NatGraph := fun {M N : Bimod}
      (T : TensorFunctor M) (S : TensorFunctor N) =>
    { G : ∀ X : AMod, Component T S X → Prop //
      (∀ X : AMod, ∃! k : Component T S X, G X k) ∧
      (∀ (X Y : AMod) (h : ModuleCat.Hom X Y)
          (k : Component T S X) (l : Component T S Y),
        G X k → G Y l →
        LinearMap.comp (ModuleCat.Hom.hom (S.1.1.map h)) k =
          LinearMap.comp l (ModuleCat.Hom.hom (T.1.1.map h))) }
  let Unitor := fun {M : Bimod} (T : TensorFunctor M) =>
    LinearEquiv (RingHom.id B) (T.1.1.obj (regular)) M.1
  let IsUnitor := fun {M : Bimod} {T : TensorFunctor M}
      (rho : Unitor T) =>
    (∀ (m : ↥M.1) (a : A), rho (T.1.2 (regular) m (ULift.up a)) = right M m a) ∧
    (∀ m : ↥M.1, rho.symm m = T.1.2 (regular) m (ULift.up (1 : A)))
  let eval := fun {M N : Bimod} {T : TensorFunctor M}
      {S : TensorFunctor N} (rho : Unitor T) (sigma : Unitor S)
      (k : Component T S (regular)) =>
    LinearMap.comp sigma.toLinearMap (LinearMap.comp k rho.symm.toLinearMap)
  let Pure := fun {M N : Bimod} {T : TensorFunctor M}
      {S : TensorFunctor N} (f : NatCode M N) (X : AMod)
      (k : Component T S X) =>
    ∀ (m : ↥M.1) (y : X), k (T.1.2 X m y) = S.1.2 X (f.1 m) y
  let Represents := fun {M N : Bimod}
      {T : TensorFunctor M} {S : TensorFunctor N}
      (rho : Unitor T) (sigma : Unitor S) (eta : NatGraph T S) (f : NatCode M N) =>
    (∀ k : Component T S (regular), eta.1 (regular) k →
      f.1 = eval rho sigma k ∧
      ∀ m : ↥M.1, f.1 m = sigma (k (T.1.2 (regular) m (ULift.up (1 : A))))) ∧
    (∀ (X : AMod) (k : Component T S X), eta.1 X k → Pure f X k)
  let InverseAssignments := fun {M N : Bimod}
      {T : TensorFunctor M} {S : TensorFunctor N}
      (rho : Unitor T) (sigma : Unitor S) =>
    (∀ eta : NatGraph T S, ∃! f : NatCode M N, Represents rho sigma eta f) ∧
    (∀ f : NatCode M N, ∃! eta : NatGraph T S, Represents rho sigma eta f)
  let Addition := fun {M N : Bimod}
      {T : TensorFunctor M} {S : TensorFunctor N}
      (rho : Unitor T) (sigma : Unitor S) =>
    ∀ eta theta : NatGraph T S,
      ∃ sum : NatGraph T S,
        (∀ (X : AMod) (k l : Component T S X),
          eta.1 X k → theta.1 X l → sum.1 X (k + l)) ∧
        (∀ (k l : Component T S (regular)),
          eta.1 (regular) k → theta.1 (regular) l →
          eval rho sigma (k + l) = eval rho sigma k + eval rho sigma l)
  let Identity := fun {M : Bimod} {T : TensorFunctor M}
      (rho : Unitor T) =>
    ∃ identity : NatGraph T T,
      (∀ X : AMod, identity.1 X LinearMap.id) ∧
      eval rho rho LinearMap.id = LinearMap.id
  let Composition := fun {M N P : Bimod}
      {T : TensorFunctor M} {S : TensorFunctor N}
      {U : TensorFunctor P}
      (rho : Unitor T) (sigma : Unitor S) (tau : Unitor U) =>
    ∀ (eta : NatGraph T S) (theta : NatGraph S U),
      ∃ composite : NatGraph T U,
        (∀ (X : AMod) (k : Component T S X) (l : Component S U X),
          eta.1 X k → theta.1 X l → composite.1 X (LinearMap.comp l k)) ∧
        (∀ (k : Component T S (regular)) (l : Component S U (regular)),
          eta.1 (regular) k → theta.1 (regular) l →
          eval rho tau (LinearMap.comp l k) =
            LinearMap.comp (eval sigma tau l) (eval rho sigma k))
  ∀ (M N P : Bimod) (T : TensorFunctor M) (S : TensorFunctor N) (U : TensorFunctor P),
    ∃ (rho : Unitor T) (sigma : Unitor S) (tau : Unitor U),
      IsUnitor rho ∧ IsUnitor sigma ∧ IsUnitor tau ∧
      InverseAssignments rho sigma ∧ InverseAssignments sigma tau ∧ InverseAssignments rho tau ∧
      Addition rho sigma ∧ Identity rho ∧ Composition rho sigma tau
sourceReason:
Alphabeta Math, Natural transformations between tensor functors are bimodule maps, Statement (thm-natural-transformations-of-tensor-functors-are-bimodule-maps), is the selected endpoint in item.portal. https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-natural-transformations-of-tensor-functors-are-bimodule-maps

The tensor universal property is pointwise existence and uniqueness. A natural transformation is expressed by the graph of its components, with a unique B-linear map at each object and the usual naturality equations. The bimodule maps are the set codes for these graphs. The shared-slot check in EndpointAudit.lean verified the full proposition and the graph of an ordinary Lean natural transformation. Both axiom audits report propext and Quot.sound, with no Classical.choice.

The 27 November owner clarification in input.request, recorded in owner-clarification.json and in the owner recheck evidence translation-rechecks-f13b4bd8ba9fe139.json, requires termwise eligibility in finite C-linear dot labels. This endpoint quantifies over all (B,A)-bimodule maps.

Ian Xiao’s related Theorem 1.1 appears on printed page 2 of the archived source/mackey-bimodules.pdf (SHA-256 bc57d13777e7df145b6dfd84029e0e9539fedb33d22b2823e14c096e4c3c12f2). The separately retrieved 27 November revision also places Theorem 1.1 on printed page 2 (SHA-256 6d7e885955f23ae6d10d8e8394d3fe9252dfc2fa7ce7ec149ec190de766c978e). Both article passages provide context. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/mackey-bimodules.pdf
